items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: we went to the Notre Dame Jazz Festival that year with Jamey and a group that included Everett Hoffman on tenor saxophone, Dickie Washburn on trumpet, myself...

ctx.x: Yeah, because he liked your writing very much. I was just curious where he had first heard your writing.

I’m not sure he liked the writing all that much, but it was part of filling up what the band had to do. So, we played that. And, oh, I’ve got to tell you one of the funniest stories I can ever remember. When we were in the Five Spot the first time – [the] Five Spot was owned by the Termini brothers. They owned the Five Spot and they owned the Jazz Gallery. The Five Spot is 5 Cooper Square. Two blocks down and around the corner was where the Jazz Gallery was. We’re playing at the Five Spot, and [Thelonious] Monk…
Of course starting a string instrument when you’re older . . .
